title: Inconsistent Nested Lock Acquisition Order
pattern: Concurrent paths acquire overlapping sets of locks in inconsistent order, including opposite-direction traversal of a linked data structure (such as a list or tree) while locking nodes incrementally.
why_bad: It violates the global partial-order invariant required for deadlock-free lock acquisition: each thread can hold a lock the other needs, creating a cyclic wait. When traversal direction determines locking order, the cycle arises dynamically from opposite-direction walks.
detection: Look for nested lock acquisitions across different threads or functions where the sequence of lock identifiers is reversed or inconsistent. Also flag multi-node traversals that retain a node lock while acquiring the next node's lock along opposite node references across different threads; two traversals in different directions without overlapping held locks are not a hit.
counterexample: All nested acquisitions obey a strict acyclic global hierarchy (e.g., always locking in alphabetical or address order); hand-over-hand traversals where all threads consistently follow that hierarchy from root/head to leaf/tail.
source: Herlihy 9.4, Paul McKenney 7.1.1, Clean Code Ch 13; Herlihy Figure 9.10
